prompt: If $x + 2y = 11$ and $3x - y = 5$, what is the value of $2x - y$?
hint: Solve the system, then build the requested expression.

hints.text: Solve the system, then build the requested expression.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a smaller system: $x + y = 5$ and $x - y = 1$ give $x = 3$, $y = 2$, so $2x - y = 4$. Solve completely first, then build whatever combination the question asks for.
From the second equation, $y = 3x - 5$. Substitute into the first.

learningObjective: Solve a system and evaluate a compound expression.
explanation: Substitute into the first: $x + 2(3x - 5) = 11$, so $x + 6x - 10 = 11$ and $7x = 21$, giving $x = 3$.

alternativeExplanations.title: The trap answers
steps: $x = 3$ and $y = 4$ will both appear among the choices, as will $x + y = 7$.
The question asks for $2x - y$ — a quantity you only reach by doing one more step after solving.
Writing the requested expression at the top of your scratch work keeps you from stopping one step early.
